correctness.rationale: The standard exponential [k/3] denominator with t=k+1 is 1-3z/(t+2)+3z²/[(t+1)(t+2)]-z³/[t(t+1)(t+2)]. Translation z=t+x gives t(t+1)(t+2)q(t+x)=2t-3tx-x³. The strictly increasing cubic x³+3tx=2t has u between 1/2 and 2/3; the roots R=t+u and Z=t-u/2+i sqrt(3t+3u²/4), conjugate Z, are simple. Their moduli obey |Z|²-R²=3t(1-u)>0. The partial-fraction coefficient of (1-z/R)^-1 is A=|Z|²/|R-Z|²>0, while the sum of two complex residue moduli is 2|B|=R|Z|/[v|R-Z|]. Exact symbolic factoring reduces A>2|B| to the positive cubic u³-4u²+10u-4 on (1/2,2/3), with positive multiplier 9u⁴(1-u)/[4(2-3u)²]. The n-th coefficient is at least R^-n(A-2|B|)>0 for all k,n. SymPy checked both factorizations exactly; independent rational recurrence checked k<=80,n<=100. No numerical cutoff is used to establish the all-order result.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Scardino's Theorem 3.1 fully covers k=0 for every odd m, and Theorem 8.2 covers positive tails for general k under property D1; Theorem 9.1 gives transient Hermite profiles and m=5 failures. None deduces the uniform residue inequality A>2|B| for all k at m=3, which closes the finite initial index region as well.

originality.rationale: Fasi–Higham 2019 pose positivity for all odd m, without proving even this fixed cubic case. The full 2026 Scardino arXiv text proves full positivity for k=0 at arbitrary odd m and eventual positivity for general k under spectral minimality, but no theorem of all-index positivity for every k at m=3. The present uniform real-residue domination is an additional quantified all-k/all-n result; it is not the already-known partial-fraction identity.
residual_risks: A separately published special-function/cubic recurrence identity proving all-index positivity for every k might exist unindexed.
The original 2019 Fasi–Higham paper was compared through the accurately reproduced conjecture rather than full original article.

value.rationale: Closes a natural smallest nontrivial unresolved odd-denominator case of an explicitly motivated numerical-linear-algebra conjecture, despite the known general failure at degree five. Uniform all-index strict inequality over arbitrary numerator order is a substantive sharp positive region, not just finite positive checks, and the strict gap identifies a robust analytic mechanism.

limitations: Only scalar reciprocal [k/3] denominator; not matrix-entry positivity or stability.
Strict residue bound decays relatively as k grows; no uniform numerical conditioning claim.
